label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is TRUE POSITIVE: User input flows from cookie -> param -> bar -> fileName -> HTML output. Although encodeForHTML(fileName) is called, the surrounding string literals ('The beginning of file: ' and '' is:') are NOT encoded, creating an XSS gap. Attacker can inject '</script>' or similar payloads in the cookie that bypass the partial encoding. Alert 2 (java/path-injection) is FALSE POSITIVE: fileName construction uses TESTFILES_DIR prefix limiting path traversal scope. Alert 3 (java/error-message-exposure) is FALSE POSITIVE: Error messages go to System.out.println() not HTTP response.

evidence.note: User input flows through Base64 roundtrip into bar, then concatenated with TESTFILES_DIR to create fileName
Sink prints fileName surrounded by unencoded string literals - XSS possible via </script> injection breaking out of quotes
